articles.title: The middle path | Explaining Supreme Court’s latest verdict on post facto environmental clearances
articles.summary: The Supreme Court struck down the Centre’s 2021 Office Memorandum that allowed ex post facto environmental clearances. The court ruled that future amnesty under the Environment (Protection) Act must come from a statutory notification, not an administrative order, and only apply to projects of critical public interest. The verdict impacts how environmental clearances are granted and enforced in India.

articles.title: Rajya Sabha Passes Bill Criminalising Insult To Vande Mataram, Giving It Same Legal Protection As National Anthem
articles.summary: The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to accord Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana. The Bill amends the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, extending the Act's penal provisions to acts of intentional disrespect towards Vande Mataram. At present, the 1971 Act criminalises intentional prevention of the singing of the national anthem or causing disturbances

articles.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) ordered an investigation into a reported issue with the fuel control switch locking mechanism on Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft. The switches control fuel supply and have faced scrutiny after a past crash incident. The DGCA's action follows a crew reporting an issue post-landing.

The study found that more than 1,700 treatment sites have closed due to these cuts. Dr. Atul Gawande, USAID's assistant administrator under President Biden, discussed the report's findings and its broader implications for global health.

articles.title: Criminal gangs increasingly lure victims to work in online scam centers, UN migration agency warns
articles.summary: Criminal gangs are increasingly luring victims into working at online scam centers, where they are often trapped, have their documents seized, and are forced to participate through violence, threats, and debt bondage. The UN migration agency warns that this trend is growing, raising concerns about human trafficking and labour exploitation. The issue involves both domestic and cross-border criminal networks operating in India and other countries.

articles.title: 'Amnesia' about measles risk and low vaccination rates have helped US infections grow
articles.summary: The U.S. has seen a significant rise in measles cases in 2026 compared to 2025, with experts attributing the surge to declining vaccination rates and public amnesia about the disease's severity. Health officials warn that measles can be life-threatening, highlighting the importance of immunization. The situation may prompt discussions on vaccination policies or public health measures in countries like India, which faces similar challenges.
articles.raw_summary: The latest US data show measles cases from January to mid-July 2026 totaled more than all cases in 2025. Experts blame a fall in vaccination and warn that people have forgotten measles can be life-threatening.

articles.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
articles.summary: Lenacapavir is a new HIV prevention drug that requires only two injections per year, offering a significant improvement over daily pills for high-risk groups. Its effectiveness depends on ensuring sufficient supply and reaching the intended at-risk populations. The drug's long-term impact on reducing HIV infections in India will depend on public health policies and implementation strategies.
articles.raw_summary: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

articles.title: Should social media platforms be held accountable for what users post?
articles.summary: Parliament is reviewing whether social media platforms should be legally accountable for illegal content posted by users. Experts are divided on whether existing rules adequately address online safety without infringing on free speech. The debate centers on finding the right balance between holding platforms responsible and protecting users' rights.

articles.title: What is the AI Kill Switch Act? Why US lawmakers want the power to shut down rogue AI models
articles.summary: US lawmakers are proposing the AI Kill Switch Act, a bill that would give the government the power to shut down dangerous AI models. The legislation aims to create an emergency control framework for powerful AI systems, requiring companies to maintain intervention capabilities. This raises questions about government authority over AI and national control over advanced technology. The move could influence global AI governance, including India's approach to regulating AI.
articles.raw_summary: The proposed US legislation seeks to create an emergency control framework for some of the world's most powerful artificial intelligence systems. It could require major AI companies to maintain the ability to intervene when models become dangerous, while raising wider questions about government authority, technological dependence and national control over advanced AI.
